narrative:
The model determined that you have about a 30% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the total amount you wanted to borrow, and the status of your checking account. Both the short nine-month duration and the relatively modest 1,670 DM amount actually worked in your favor; most approved applicants request longer terms and larger sums, so these choices pushed the prediction toward good credit. Unfortunately, the status of your checking account had the opposite and ultimately decisive effect. Having a balance between 0 and 200 DM is fairly uncommon among approved applicants, and the model interpreted this as a warning sign that increased the likelihood of bad credit enough to outweigh the positive signals from the loan size and length.

In short, while your smaller, shorter-term request looked responsible, the limited funds visible in your checking account raised enough concern to tip the overall assessment against approval.

You should consider re-applying once you have built a stronger balance in a checking account or can show a longer history of steady deposits. Improving that single factor could meaningfully change how a future application is viewed. (218 words)
